negativeSpacePhilosophy.coreprinciple: 40-60% of each frame should be intentionally open for text overlay. Visuals should support, not compete with, typography.

requirements.maximum: 80% open space per slide (for quote/statement slides)

implementation.abstract-visuals: Use gradient density, line spacing, or shape placement to create clear text zones
implementation.photographic-visuals: Use depth of field, composition, and subject placement to create negative space
implementation.geometric-visuals: Place shapes intentionally to leave large open zones for text

textZoneStrategy.top-third: Best for headlines with supporting visuals below
textZoneStrategy.bottom-third: Best for body text with hero visuals above
textZoneStrategy.center: Best for bold statements with frame-edge visuals
textZoneStrategy.side-panels: Best for asymmetric layouts with vertical text
textZoneStrategy.split: Best for comparison or contrasting content

negativeSpacePhilosophy.mayvenInspiration: Sophisticated Instagram accounts like @mayven_____ use intentional negative space as a design element, not an afterthought. Space = elegance.

hierarchyZones.description: How to structure visual hierarchy to support text hierarchy

headlineZone.location: Largest negative space area (typically top-third or center)
headlineZone.colorContrast: Ensure 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum for accessibility
headlineZone.spacing: Minimum 80px from frame edges, 60px from other text layers

bodyZone.location: Secondary negative space area (typically middle or bottom-third)
bodyZone.visualTreatment: Supporting visual elements OK, but keep readable

accentZone.location: Small areas for micro-labels, numbers, or icons
accentZone.visualTreatment: Can overlap with visual elements if contrast maintained
accentZone.colorContrast: 3:1 contrast ratio minimum for accent text

logoZone.location: Consistent position across slides (typically bottom-right or top-left corner)
logoZone.visualTreatment: Always on clean background, never obscured
logoZone.spacing: Minimum 60px from edges, 40px from other elements

hierarchyZones.integration: Visuals should create natural zones for each hierarchy level through composition, color, and depth

colorFlow.description: How to create visual continuity through color across carousel slides

brandColorUsage.primary: Use as dominant color in 60-70% of slides
brandColorUsage.secondary: Use as supporting color in 30-40% of slides
brandColorUsage.accent: Use sparingly for emphasis and CTA slides
brandColorUsage.strategy: Maintain brand color presence while allowing variation in treatment

transitionStrategy.consistent-palette: All slides use same color palette with different compositions
transitionStrategy.progressive-shift: Gradually shift color emphasis across slides (light to dark, cool to warm)
transitionStrategy.contrasting-punctuation: Most slides consistent, 1-2 slides use contrasting colors for impact
transitionStrategy.recommendation: Choose based on carousel narrative and visual complexity

socialNativePalette.usage: Mix with brand colors for contemporary, social-native feel

gradientStrategy.direction: Vertical for calm/sophisticated, diagonal for dynamic, radial for focus
gradientStrategy.recommendation: Match complexity to brand personality and content type

typographyIntegration.description: How visuals should support (not compete with) text overlay

minimal-background.description: Visual serves purely as background canvas for text
minimal-background.visualComplexity: Very low - gradients, subtle textures, simple shapes
minimal-background.textDominance: High - text is the primary design element

supporting-visual.description: Visual adds context and interest without dominating
supporting-visual.visualComplexity: Medium - icons, simple compositions, abstract forms
supporting-visual.textDominance: Balanced - text and visual share importance

hero-visual.description: Strong visual impact with strategic text placement
hero-visual.visualComplexity: High - photography, complex compositions, bold imagery
hero-visual.textDominance: Low to medium - visual leads, text supports

textPlacementGuidelines.onSimpleBackgrounds: Center or asymmetric placement, large bold typography
textPlacementGuidelines.onComplexBackgrounds: Use negative space zones identified in visual, add text shadows for readability
textPlacementGuidelines.onPhotography: Place text in blur zones, sky, clean walls, or use overlay for contrast
textPlacementGuidelines.onAbstractVisuals: Align text with visual flow direction, use color contrast from composition

textEffects.shadows: Use for text on complex backgrounds (20-40px blur, 40-60% opacity)
textEffects.overlays: Semi-transparent color overlay behind text (40-80% opacity)

typographyIntegration.mayvenApproach: Bold, oversized typography is a primary design element. Text doesn't just sit on the visual - it's integrated into the composition as a graphic element.

slideToSlideTransitions.description: How visuals create narrative flow across carousel slides

consistent-theme.description: All slides use same visual style with minor variations
consistent-theme.implementation: Same style from library, different compositions or color emphasis
consistent-theme.example: All slides use gradient-atmosphere with different color combinations

evolving-story.description: Visual style evolves to support narrative progression
evolving-story.implementation: Start with hero visual, transition to cleaner typography-led slides
evolving-story.example: Slide 1: editorial-photography, Slides 2-4: geometric-minimal, Slide 5: gradient-atmosphere

contrasting-punctuation.description: Mostly consistent with strategic visual contrast for emphasis
contrasting-punctuation.implementation: 3-4 slides consistent, 1 slide bold contrast for key message
contrasting-punctuation.bestFor: Any carousel with a key slide that needs emphasis
contrasting-punctuation.example: Slides 1-3: abstract-flows in muted tones, Slide 4: duotone-abstract in bold contrast for CTA

continuityElements.colorThread: Consistent brand color appears in every slide (even if minimal)
continuityElements.visualMotif: Repeated shape, line style, or graphic element across slides
continuityElements.lightingTreatment: If using photography, maintain consistent lighting mood
continuityElements.compositionalRhythm: Alternate between dense and sparse compositions for visual rhythm
continuityElements.textZoneConsistency: Keep text zones in similar positions for cohesive feel

transitionTiming.slide1: Hook - strongest visual impact (hero-visual or bold abstract)
transitionTiming.slide2-3: Build - supporting visuals that explain or develop (supporting-visual)
transitionTiming.slide4: Peak - key insight or proof (can be hero-visual or impactful abstract)
transitionTiming.rationale: Visual intensity should follow narrative arc: impact → support → impact → resolution

avoidPatterns.randomStyleMixing: Don't use 5 different styles with no connection
avoidPatterns.monotonicRepetition: Don't use identical visuals on every slide
avoidPatterns.competingFocalPoints: Don't have multiple strong visuals fighting for attention
avoidPatterns.inconsistentColorStory: Don't jump between unrelated color palettes

mayvenEditorialPrinciples.description: Core design philosophy extracted from sophisticated Instagram editorial accounts

principles.humanCentered: Prefer lifestyle photography showing real contexts over abstract scenes or stock imagery when appropriate
principles.typographyAsDesign: Bold, oversized typography is a design element, not just information delivery
principles.playfulReferences: Contemporary UI elements, collage effects, and social-native motifs are welcome
principles.controlledPalette: Bright or pastel accents used strategically, never chaotic or overwhelming
principles.intentionalSpace: Negative space is a deliberate design choice, creating elegance and breathing room
principles.cohesiveVariety: Each slide feels unique but part of a cohesive art direction
principles.socialNativeAesthetic: Relatable, aspirational, modern - designed for Instagram, not transplanted from print

bannedElements.neonWireframes: No neon line icons, dark grid overlays, or technical wireframes
bannedElements.corporateCliche: No black-and-gold luxury aesthetic or generic corporate stock imagery
bannedElements.blueprintUI: No technical diagrams, app UI mockups, or blueprint grids
bannedElements.clipArtDocuments: No floating document icons, generic paper stacks, or office clip art
bannedElements.unrelatedScenes: Each slide should connect to the content, not be randomly generated
bannedElements.busyPatterns: Avoid complex repeating patterns that compete with text

slideTypeBalance.recommendation: For 3-5 slide carousels: 1-2 IMAGE-LED slides (hero visuals) + remaining TYPOGRAPHY-LED slides (clean backgrounds)

imageLed.purpose: Hook, emotional impact, product showcase, scene setting
imageLed.treatment: Lifestyle photography or bold abstract with strong composition
imageLed.textOverlay: Minimal text, large headlines, strategic placement

typographyLed.textOverlay: Text is the hero, visual supports without distraction

slideTypeBalance.rationale: Balance visual impact with content delivery. Not every slide needs a complex visual.

beforeGeneration: Identify content type and select appropriate style from library
Determine if slide is IMAGE-LED or TYPOGRAPHY-LED
Plan negative space zones based on text hierarchy
Choose brand colors and accent palette
Define visual continuity elements across slides
duringGeneration: Verify prompt includes NO TEXT instruction
Specify exact negative space zones and percentages
Add technical quality requirements (high resolution, 1:1 aspect ratio)
afterGeneration: Validate negative space zones are clear and usable
Verify no text, logos, or readable characters in image
Check contrast for text overlay zones (4.5:1 minimum)
Ensure visuals support (not compete with) intended text

successMetrics.negativeSpaceAdequacy: 50%+ of frame available for text overlay
successMetrics.visualContinuity: Carousel feels cohesive, branded, intentionally designed
successMetrics.textReadability: All text meets 4.5:1 contrast ratio on visual backgrounds
successMetrics.brandAlignment: Visuals reflect brand personality and industry appropriately
successMetrics.socialNativeAesthetic: Carousel looks Instagram-native, not AI-generated or corporate
successMetrics.contentSupport: Visuals enhance understanding, don't distract from message
successMetrics.noTextInImages: Zero generated images contain text, logos, or readable characters
